steps.content: [Scene Change: Office]
Bad luck has shadowed Murphy from the moment she entered this world. It's just her everyday reality.
In the beginning, it wasn't the catastrophic kind of disaster. More often, it's just the smallest, most ridiculous little accidents, the kind you'd feel silly even bringing up.
But somehow, they always, always picked her.
Murphy stares at the files scattered over her desk, a couple of unopened snack bags, and that familiar phone sitting right there.
Wait... is she back? Just as the celebration is about to begin in her head, a voice cuts through the air and reaches her.
Murphy, where are the materials you prepared?

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: Oh, the materials, right... the materials...
Murphy digs through her bag, pats down every corner, and finally flips the whole thing inside out. Still, the papers she stayed up finishing last night are nowhere in sight.
...If those papers don't turn up today, don't bother turning up tomorrow either.

The person in front of her radiates a quiet, imposing authority. Murphy breaks out in a cold sweat and shoves her hand back into the bag for another desperate search. Maybe, just maybe, fortune is finally on her side; her fingers brush against something that feels exactly like a sheet of paper.

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: —HAH! Got it! Take that, universe! The curse on me is officially broken. Today is the day my luck turns around!
Murphy eagerly unfolds the paper, only to find it's nothing but a comic strip.
Inside, there's a cape-wearing ranger, a warrior dragging a lamppost behind her, a rabbit forever on the run, a calm and collected analyst, and a worker in gray overalls.
And a little slip of paper, fluttering down.
All you ever bring is bad luck to everyone else.

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: ...Wait, what?!
[Scene Change: Dungeon - Can use Happyzoo Restaurant background]
Murphy opens her eyes and finds herself surrounded by familiar sights. After confirming it was all just a dream, she heaves a huge sigh of relief.

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: Oh, thank god... just a dream. For a second there I thought I'd screwed up again...
But just a few seconds later, she sees something that makes even less sense. Pink dust is swirling everywhere, and everyone caught in it is acting like they've been hexed.

steps.speaker: EMP
steps.content: Morning, everyone! So I've been thinking, really thinking, and I've come to a very important conclusion. I am, without a doubt, a very important person!
EMP, acting like a total drunk, just goes off and starts putting on her own little show.

steps.speaker: EMP
steps.content: I'm either the main character or one of those scene-stealing powerhouses who shows up and just owns the first three minutes. Honestly? Leaning toward the latter. It's more my style.

steps.speaker: Letta
steps.content: No, no, no. Letta is the best one! Letta can do anything now. Anyone tries to stop Letta? Squish. Flat. Like a pancake.

Letta heaves her arm upward like she's lifting something impossibly heavy, though the lantern is already back in her hand. She just hasn't realized yet; she still thinks she's exactly the same as she was yesterday.

steps.speaker: EMP
steps.content: Girl, you're giving off total villain energy. Can't you take some notes from me? Elegance. A little elegance, please.

steps.speaker: Lynn
steps.content: No, that's not right... I keep feeling like I'm supposed to run forward first, and then turn left, and then fall into a hole...

steps.speaker: Lynn
steps.content: But... why would I fall into a hole?

Each of them rambles on, talking away to themselves, like they've slipped into some strange alternate reality where they've become entirely different people, performing acts no ordinary mind could comprehend.

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: Guys? What's... what's going on with you all?
Out of all of them, Murphy is the most clear-headed. When she sees her friends acting so strange, she hurries over, worried, and asks if they're okay.
You let out a sigh. The shackles flicker with a faint glow.

Crimson patterns crawl up EMP's gloves and along her sleeves. The dark haze veiling her form scatters swiftly, then, with a crisp, shattering sound, breaks apart into a cascade of shimmering motes. In an instant, clarity returns to her eyes.

steps.speaker: EMP
steps.content: Huh?!

steps.speaker: EMP
steps.content: Wha—no! I was this close to going up on stage at the DisCars! I could literally see Director Deren handing me the award herself!
Next are Letta and Lynn. One by one, you dispel the affliction that has taken hold of them.
Murphy seems perfectly fine, yet you reach out with the shackles and touch her anyway.
The moment they make contact, thin tendrils of dark mist rise from her body, unfurling and spreading like living things, as though locked in a silent struggle against the shackles' power.

You withdraw the shackles' power, and the dark mist fades with it, vanishing into nothing. Murphy stands frozen, staring at the scene before her. Even someone as slow on the uptake as she is can grasp what has just unfolded.
Yesterday, the ability deviation among the Sinners could still be laughed off as a curious little amusement to brighten the day. But today, their very consciousness has been thrown into disarray.

steps.speaker: EMP
steps.content: Okay, someone say something! Why did everyone just go quiet all of a sudden?
EMP wants to say something to cut through the silence, but nobody here is clueless. They can all tell that Mania's influence has gotten stronger.
And if it worsens just a little more? Will they all be lost in this realm forever?

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: ...This is me, isn't it? This whole mess... It's gotta be my ability.

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: But... if it really is my ability, shouldn't I be the first one going crazy? So why's it hitting everyone else instead...?

steps.speaker: Lynn
steps.content: ...Even if it's Murphy's ability doing this... it's dangerous, yes, but... it's not too late. There has to be a way to fix it!

steps.speaker: Lynn
steps.content: If everyone starts avoiding her because of this... she'd be so hurt...

steps.speaker: Lynn
steps.content: Just like I was...

steps.speaker: Lynn & Murphy
steps.content:
—I have an idea!
—So I was thinking...
After the silence has stretched on long enough, Lynn and Murphy both open their mouths at almost the same moment, only to stop themselves just as abruptly.

steps.speaker: Lynn & Murphy
steps.content:
—You go first!
—You first!
Lynn seems on the verge of speaking, but the words catch in her throat and she swallows them back down. Murphy parts her lips, yet in the end she only lowers her head further.
Just then, the crisp sound of footsteps rings out from the far end of the cavern. A calm, measured female voice follows.
It seems like... you could use a hand.
You follow the voice to its source and find Norma, just returned from completing her investigation.

steps.speaker: Norma
steps.content: This one's fairly simple to solve, actually. Think of it like noise reduction.

steps.speaker: Norma
steps.content: You can shield the receiver, block the transmission, or... control the noise right at the source.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: At the source?

Norma produces a folding blackboard as if from thin air, snaps it open with practiced efficiency, and hangs it upon the wall. She then raps it sharply with her weapon, like a teacher with a pointer, commanding everyone's attention.
[Small CG 1: Norma]

steps.speaker: Norma
steps.content: We've confirmed that Murphy's anomalous concept has interfered with the Mania field, warping it into what we're seeing now.

steps.speaker: Norma
steps.content: The scope of her ability is considerable. It affects those around her, the surrounding environment, and even... Murphy herself.

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: It's... it's not that crazy, is it?
[Small CG 2: Norma]
Norma taps the blackboard, and the image of Murphy upon it begins to shift and change at a dizzying speed.

It starts with a stumble, a fall. Then comes a flowerpot plummeting onto her head, followed by slime clinging to her, magic blasts hurtling her way, and at last, a frantic, breathless flight from some unknown creatures...

steps.speaker: Lynn
steps.content: So... as long as we can't find that experimental substance triggering the Mania, Murphy just... keeps going through all of this?

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: S-sorry... I didn't mean to...
What's our best option right now, then?
Before you can finish, Norma has already pulled up her solution.
[Small CG 3: Norma]

steps.speaker: Norma
steps.content: That would be... <color=#fb9259>tying Murphy and Chief together.</color>

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: ...Huh?

steps.speaker: Norma
steps.content: Correct.
Norma nods in affirmation, then picks up her pointer once more to resume her analysis.

steps.speaker: Norma
steps.content: ${PlayerName}'s shackles provide the most stable suppressive and corrective response to anomalies. They won't erase her misfortune entirely, but sustained close contact should at least reduce her interference with the Mania field to manageable levels.
Murphy goes rigid, her entire body locking up with a tension so fierce she cannot move. It seems this is the first time she has ever been in such close proximity to another person.

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: Y-you really don't have to go this far for me!

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: And! Chief... if my misfortune is never going away...

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: No. Leaving you unaccounted for risks even more unpredictable and dangerous outcomes.
[Scene Change]
Seeing that everyone has grasped the method, Norma packs away her full set of teaching tools.
But your mind drifts back to the feedback you felt when the shackles touched Murphy earlier, and a better idea begins to take shape.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Murphy's ability affects everyone around her, right? So what if we point it in the right direction instead of just blocking it?

steps.speaker: Norma
steps.content: You mean... targeted induction?
Norma does not consider this the wisest course of action, but you still your mind regardless and direct the shackles to fasten around Murphy's wrist.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Here's the plan: I'll keep a light connection, just enough to stay linked without pushing back against your misfortune. But when we're in a fight, I'll use the shackles to stimulate it.
When that happens, I need you to genuinely wish the enemy well.

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: ...Wait, what? What do you mean?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: We want your bad luck to work against the Mania. That's how your ability really shines.
Think of it like this, you root for an enemy to stand their ground, and they will trip instead.

steps.speaker: Norma
steps.content: ...Using the shackles as a conduit to direct intent onto enemy targets. The theory checks out, but it'll demand sharp focus. If your concentration slips...

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I'll keep an eye on her.

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: This still sounds completely insane...

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: But... if it's you asking, Chief... Okay! I-I'll give it everything I've got!

steps.speaker: Norma
steps.content: Then I'd best be going as well.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Where to?

steps.speaker: Norma
steps.content: I'll continue the analysis. Time to figure out what's really happening to this space.
